Abstract.AbstractText: Peri-prosthetic humerus fractures are a relatively uncommon occurrence that can be difficult to manage non-operatively. Locking plate technology has enhanced the surgical management of these fractures. However, adequate fixation around the stem remains of some concern. We describe an osteosynthesis technique utilizing a locking plate utilizing eccentrically placed screw holes to place "skive screws" in the proximal end of the plate to achieve fixation around the stem of the implant. A clinical series of five consecutive patients treated with this technique is presented with an average follow-up of 29 months (range 12-48). Two additional patients had less than 1-year follow-up. All patients demonstrated fracture healing. Functional outcomes were limited with only one patient achieving forward elevation above 90 degrees and average ASES Function score was 28. Pain relief was nearly uniform with an average VAS pain score of 0.5.
